title: Warehouse and BI
for: the data warehouse, transformation layer, BI dashboards, CDP and reverse ETL that hold the joined marketing data

manual.export: Run the question in the BI tool or warehouse console and export the result as CSV.
manual.drop: export the query result as CSV into the matching data/<domain>/snapshots/

vendors.name: dbt
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__dbt`) until checked
The CLI toolset runs `dbt build`/`run` against the warehouse; set DISABLE_DBT_CLI=true and DISABLE_SQL=true to keep the server to the semantic layer and discovery.
A hosted server exists on the dbt platform (URL is per account, token plus production environment id); wire it from the account's settings page when the local package is not wanted.
Pinned to dbt-mcp 2.2.1 (PyPI, checked 2026-09-04).

auth.where: dbt platform > Account settings > Service tokens; the production environment id from the environment page

cli.install: pip install dbt-core plus the warehouse adapter, or the dbt platform CLI
cli.notes: `dbt show` and `dbt sl query` for scripted metric pulls; runs unattended with a service token

vendors.name: Snowflake
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__snowflake`) until checked

The Snowflake-managed MCP server (GA November 2025) is created per database and schema, so its URL is account-specific; SNOWFLAKE_MCP_URL holds it. Auth by programmatic access token or OAuth; the bearer form here follows the Snowflake REST convention, confirm on the docs.
SQL runs with the connecting role's grants; use a read-only role for marketing pulls.
A local alternative exists (snowflake-labs-mcp 1.4.2 on PyPI, `uvx snowflake-labs-mcp==1.4.2`); it needs a tools config file, so it is not listed as an entry.

auth.where: Snowsight > Admin > Users > Programmatic access tokens; the server URL from the MCP server object in your database

cli.notes: `snow sql -q ... --format csv` for scheduled exports with a service user

vendors.name: BigQuery
caveats: SQL runs with the principal's IAM roles; grant BigQuery Data Viewer and Job User only, so DML cannot happen.
Google OAuth in the browser; for unattended pulls use the `bq` CLI with a service account.
Also the documented path for Dreamdata (Data Warehouse add-on) and for GA4 raw exports.
The MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/genai-toolbox) is the self-hosted alternative.

auth.where: Google account grant in the browser on first use

cli.install: part of the Google Cloud SDK (gcloud)
cli.notes: `bq query --format=csv --use_legacy_sql=false '...'` with a service account for scheduled pulls

vendors.name: Looker
caveats: The Looker-managed server is per instance, so LOOKER_BASE_URL holds the instance URL; the `/mcp` path and OAuth flow are from secondary listings, confirm on the docs page.
Reads only, within the user's Looker permissions.

auth.where: browser grant on first use; LOOKER_BASE_URL is the instance URL

vendors.name: Metabase
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__metabase`) until checked
Built into Metabase since version 60 at `<your metabase>/api/metabase-mcp`; METABASE_URL holds the instance URL. Permissions follow the Metabase user; an API key inherits its creator's group.
The `x-api-key` header is the Metabase API convention; confirm the MCP endpoint accepts it (session cookies may be required in some versions).

auth.where: Metabase > Admin > Settings > Authentication > API keys

vendors.name: Tableau
capabilities: query a data source (VizQL Data Service)
caveats: Hosted server at https://mcp.tableau.com with OAuth 2.1 (Tableau Cloud); the local package runs against Tableau Server or Cloud with a personal access token and is the headless route.
Pinned to @tableau/mcp-server 4.8.1 (npm, checked 2026-09-04).

auth.where: Tableau > My Account Settings > Personal Access Tokens

vendors.name: Power BI
caveats: The remote server is in public preview with Entra ID auth and its endpoint is tenant-specific; not listed until a person confirms it in the Fabric admin portal.
The local package (@microsoft/powerbi-modeling-mcp, 0.5.0-beta.13 on npm) is a modeling tool for Power BI Desktop, writes to semantic models, and is not a reporting route; excluded on purpose.
For marketing pulls, query the underlying warehouse instead.

vendors.name: Dreamdata
caveats: A Dreamdata MCP Server was announced on 1 September 2026; the documented path today is the Google BigQuery managed MCP over the Dreamdata Data Warehouse add-on. Wire `bigquery` in this file and query the Dreamdata dataset.
The Data Warehouse add-on is required.

vendors.name: Segment
caveats: No official server as of May 2026. The community `segment-mcp` package only sends track/identify calls, which is a write, not a read; community server maintained by an individual; judge as a script, not a vendor tool.
Read Segment data from the warehouse it syncs to.

vendors.name: RudderStack
caveats: write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__rudderstack`) until checked
Public beta; 30+ tools including configuration writes. Seen in secondary listings only.

vendors.name: Hightouch
caveats: Must be enabled by Hightouch for the workspace (not self-serve); the endpoint is issued at enablement, so no entry is listed.
The server is read/write (audiences, syncs, journeys) under workspace RBAC; ask for a read-only role before wiring.

vendors.name: Census
caveats: Acquired by Fivetran in 2025; no MCP server found. Read the synced data in the destination tool instead.
